# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why5: These keep my pitch: notes done during the walk instead of hours after it, and texting the crew action items, with no number I didn't write.
screens.why7: Both rows are kept in order and joined with 'and', and neither is something the trailer upload already gives. But the belief's moment, 'the last time they sat in the trailer uploading photos', is the routine end of the day rather than the moment it cost them. A super whose upload went quickly that day could fairly answer 'no difference', which bends the card's hard-case rule.
screens.instead: Keep both rows, but have the belief read: For most, with it, the last time the daily log took the rest of their evening would have given them hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day.

screens.why1: Right after I typed what Fresco does better, I'm checking how Keel reworded my benefits and the belief it will test, which is exactly where this belongs.
screens.why2: "Hours back at the end of the day" and "action items to the crew the same day" are how a super or I would say it, with nothing from outside the trade.
screens.why3: Both gains are things a superintendent lives every day: the hours in the trailer after the walks and getting punch items to the crew before they leave.
screens.why4: Two distinct rows, each under nine words, one about time and one about getting items to the crew, with no overlap and nothing silly.
screens.why5: The rows still say what I pitch: the 90% faster notes and texting the crew action items, with my lead benefit kept first.
screens.why7: The belief carries both benefits joined with "and" in my order, but its hard case, "the last time they sat in the trailer uploading photos", is the daily routine rather than the moment it cost them, a super who got through it fine would answer "no difference", so it bends the card's hard-case rule.
screens.instead: Same two rows, but have Keel test: For most, with it, the last time the daily log ate their evening after the walks would have given them hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day.

screens.why1: After fit and advantage, asking what effort my supers take on to start is the obvious last solution question before the price.
screens.why2: Setup, extra steps, learning, up to four of nine words each: I can answer it on first read in my own words.
screens.why3: I know what a super has to change on the walk and before the notes go to the crew, from our own users.
screens.why4: The only chip is the escape, and 'I'm not sure', leaving the dimension out, fits a founder who can't name the effort.
screens.why5: My two rows are kept as I'd say them: name who owns each item as they film, and check and fix the notes before they go out.
screens.why7: Both rows are steps the super takes themselves, base-form verbs in their voice, within nine words, distinct, and clear of Compatibility's film-and-talk and of Purchase friction; the one escape is there as the card requires.

screens.why1: Right after I said what they'd have to do to start, Keel shows me the efforts back as rows to check, which is the obvious next step before I pick one to test.
screens.why2: 'Name who owns each item as they film' and 'Check and fix the notes before they go out' are how a super talks about punch items and notes going to the crew and to Procore.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does on their own walk and in their own trailer: saying who's on the corroded beam, and reading the notes before they're sent.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, one during the walk and one after it, in my words with no overlap, and the '1 to 4 efforts' guidance fits a list I can still add to.
screens.why5: The owner-naming row is my own launch example ('needs replacement by Alex'), and checking the notes answers the hallucination worry I heard in the thread, so it still means what I typed.
screens.why7: Each row is one effort under 9 words, a base-form verb in 'they' voice, and a step the super takes themselves; neither repeats Compatibility's filming-on-the-walk or a Purchase-friction sign-off, so a Yes or a Probably not would answer the belief either way.

screens.why1: Right after I checked my adoption-effort rows, picking the one most likely to stop a super is the obvious next step before Keel writes the test.
screens.why2: Naming who owns each item and checking notes before they go out are how a super already talks about punch items and the log, so it reads at first glance.
screens.why3: Both are things a super would do on their own walk and in their own log, so they can answer from their own day.
screens.why4: The two efforts are distinct, both are real catches (saying the assignee aloud while filming; reviewing what the AI wrote before it goes to the crew or Procore), and filming and talking itself is already tested on Compatibility, so nothing is missing here.
screens.why5: My pick is kept word for word and matches my pitch, where the super says the owner aloud as they film ('needs replacement by Alex') and Fresco turns it into assignees.
screens.why7: Both rows are steps the super takes themselves, in base form with 'they', one effort each, 2 within the 1 to 4, and none repeats Compatibility or Purchase friction; the belief can go either way against Yes / Only if / Probably not / No, with I can't tell on the stranger's item.

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out is the obvious place to decide whether to collect emails from supers who'd try it on a live job, and Fresco is selling paid pilots per site, so I want those names.
screens.why2: "Offer a pilot?" with the exact line respondents will see and where I'll find the yeses is plain on first read.
screens.why3: Whether I want leads for a pilot is my own call as the founder, nothing to guess.
screens.why4: Yes or no is the complete choice here, the two options are distinct and in plain words, and no escape is needed for a founder's own decision.
screens.why5: The respondent line "Would you try this for real?" fits, but my pilot is a paid one on one site sold to the contractor, and the screen doesn't say that a superintendent's email yes is a user lead rather than a buyer commitment, so it drifts a little from what I mean by a pilot.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? People who say yes see: "Would you try this on one of your sites? Leave your email." (Yes, ask them / No pilot)

screens.why1: Saving my answers at the last step, just before strangers see the study, is plainly where this belongs.
screens.why2: The heading says 'save your answers', but the pick reads 'lock and record the face Keel preselects', and I had to read twice to work out that 'face' means the AI interviewer's look and that 'lock' means I can't change it afterwards.
screens.why3: It's my own study and my own call whether to save it with Keel's default interviewer, so I can answer it straight off.
screens.why4: The option I picked bundles three things (lock, record, accept the default face), and it isn't clear that a separate 'save but let me pick the face' or 'save and keep editing' choice sits beside it.
screens.why5: Nothing here rewords my superintendents, the daily log or the narrated-video scribe; it only saves what I typed.
screens.instead: Save your answers? Options: 'Save and use Keel's interviewer (you can't edit after this)' / 'Let me pick the interviewer first' / 'Not yet, go back and edit'

screens.why1: Choosing how the link reaches the supers is the last thing to settle before sending, so it sits right at the end after saving my answers.
screens.why2: The three options read plainly, but the bare question "New link" with the kicker "INTERVIEWS" makes me read twice to see I'm picking how strangers answer, not making a link.
screens.why3: I know my supers: phone in hand in the trailer, used to tapping through Procore forms, so I can pick this from what I know.
screens.why4: Read-and-tap, AI interviewer, or let them choose covers the real choices, each distinct and plainly described, with "Let them choose" as a fair middle.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product's wording is touched or leaked here; it is only the delivery format, and my pick "Read and tap" stands.
screens.instead: How should the superintendents answer when they open the link? -- Read and tap / An AI interviewer asks aloud / Let them choose

screens.why_b1: The verdict, Too few to call, sits under the title with its deciding number (4 counted), and each card gives the bar beside it (5 needed to call it), so I know none of the three beliefs could be called and why.
screens.why_b2: There is no chart here, but the tally (3 beliefs, 3 too few, 7 answered, 4 counted) and the bar of 5 read at once; what I cannot see is why 3 of the 7 supers were not counted.
screens.why_b3: The three dimension names are mine and the beliefs are recognisable, but the statement under the title repeats itself ('turns them into notes... and gets back notes with photos, assignees and due dates...'), and the Relative advantage line is a clumsy rewording of my 'hours back, action items the same day'.
screens.why_b4: The page tells me nothing about what to do; I am one counted answer short on every card and it never says to send the study to a few more superintendents, or how many more.
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing it cannot carry: 7 answered and 4 counted are visible, and it refuses to call any belief on 4 people.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there's no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars count answers per option, '5 answered · 4 counted' with Luis's guess as the ghost cell gives the base, and the marker at 4 of 5 squares with 'no more than 1 in 3' once five are counted.
screens.why_b3: The condition is my row word for word, but the belief drops 'on commercial jobs' from my people, and the question asks about my last 'daily log' rather than the site walk I moved the occasion to, which is where the noise actually is.
screens.why_b4: 'Ray's no is the one to ask about' gives me one concrete call to make, but the line doesn't say that one more counted answer would settle it, or what a lean of 3 for and 1 against means for filming on the walk.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said plainly ('a lean, not a call'), but asking about 'your last daily log', which my supers write in the trailer, makes the answers about noise on site softer evidence than the card implies.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know why there is no call.
screens.why_b2: I can see better versus same over 4 people, but the doubled counts ('Better · 3 3 a lot') and the bar written as '4 of 5' when only 4 were counted took me a second look to square with 'no more than 1 in 3'.
screens.why_b3: Both benefits are mine, hours back and action items to the crew the same day, but the moment is now the routine trailer upload rather than the day it went wrong. The bar line keeps only 'hours back', and the count line calls the moment 'their last daily log', so the belief reads as recognisable but reworded.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me that one more superintendent's answer would decide it, or that 3 of 4 already lean my way.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible throughout, the small group is flagged as 'a lean, not a call', Luis's guess is set apart, and nothing claims the belief held.
screens.instead: 3 of 4 supers said Fresco would have made that day a lot better and 1 said no difference (her log is done before she leaves the gate); one more answer decides it, so get one more superintendent through Part 2.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, 4 counted with 5 needed, so I know the answer and why at once.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 4 superintendents' answers, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' next to 'no more than 1 in 3 say probably not or no' takes a second look before I see the marker means 4 of 5 for, not the 4 counted.
screens.why_b3: Adoption friction and 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' are the effort I picked; the 'You said' line is clumsy but it is still my row.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say to get one more superintendent counted, or that two of my three yeses hinge on keeping crew names private, which is the thing I'd actually go fix.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, Luis's guess is set apart, and the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', so nothing claims more than four people can carry.
screens.instead: Leaning yes, 3 of 4, but 2 of those only if crew names stay private: get one more super counted and decide how Fresco handles names before you call it.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on 'Too few to call' with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right beside it, so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and Relative advantage are my dimensions, the noise line is the revised belief I checked, and the advantage line is my 'hours back' and 'action items to the crew' benefit in recognisable form.
screens.why_b4: Nothing on the screen tells me what to do: not that I need one more superintendent per line, and not what the two objections mean for the scribe.
screens.why_b5: Both lines keep the n visible (one against, one asked, four counted, short of five) and claim nothing beyond those two people.
screens.why_b6: Ray's 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' and Denise's 'log's done on the tablet before I leave the gate; schedule and subs eat my day' tell me something I did not type: on a bad day, and for a super whose way already works, the log is not the pain at all, and the schedule and subs are.
screens.instead: Too few to call, one more super needed on each line; but both who said no put the day's pain on the schedule and subs, not the log, so test that before building more of the scribe.

screens.why1: A first screen that checks whether my jobs run their daily logs in software is an obvious gate before asking about my logs.
screens.why2: I'd get it on one hearing, but I'd never say "construction project management software"; on my jobs it's just Procore or ACC, so the phrase takes a beat to map.
screens.why3: I know which platform every job I run logs in, so I can answer straight from what I do.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a gate, and a gate takes no escape.
screens.why5: It asks only about the software my jobs already use and says nothing of the founder's product or plan.
screens.why6: Heard aloud it's one short question with two options, but "construction project management software" is a five-word mouthful in the middle of the breath.
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you run keep their daily logs in software like Procore or ACC? Yes; or No.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my jobs keep logs in Procore-type software, asking whether I had to finish the log after I'd left the site is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Daily log, the site, finishing it after I leave: that's exactly how I'd say it, and I can answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: I know if I was punching in the log at the kitchen table or in the truck this week versus closing it out in the trailer before I left.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly, and the chips beside it belong to the story box after a Yes, so they don't muddy the gate.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's problem, the log spilling past the site, and nothing about an AI scribe or the founder's product reaches me.
screens.why6: It's one short question with Yes or no at the end, easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: The gate asks the costly act rather than the routine every super does (keeping a daily log), so a super who closed it out on site truly says No and one who finished it at home says Yes, and the belief can be supported or refuted with no escape, as the card requires.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether I finished my log after leaving the site, showing me a tool for the site walk is the obvious next step before the idea questions.
screens.why2: Site walk, Procore, ACC, assignees and action items are my words, but nobody on a job calls anything an "AI scribe," so that one phrase makes me stop.
screens.why3: I do site walks every day, take photos and videos, and push items to Procore and to my subs, so I can judge this from what I actually do.
screens.why4: A card to read, with no options.
screens.why5: The card drifts from the daily log I was just asked about toward walk notes and texting action items, and "your crew" doesn't fit a GC super whose work is done by subs, not a crew of my own.
screens.why6: It says well in short sentences, but the belief line re-lists what the how already said, so it's heard twice, and "AI scribe" is clumsy out loud.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an app that turns your site walk videos into your daily log. ... The people building it believe it would get your daily log done before you leave the site.

screens.why1: Right after the Fresco card, asking whether I could even talk into my phone on site is the obvious first thing to check, since the whole idea depends on it.
screens.why2: The words are mine, but 'your last daily log' is where I sit in the trailer typing, not where I'm out in the noise, so I had to read it twice to see they mean the walk that fed the log.
screens.why3: I know how loud my last pour or framing day was and whether I could have dictated over it, so I can answer that from my own day.
screens.why4: Easily, most of the time, sometimes, no is the real spread on a loud job, with 'I can't tell' apart, and nothing overlaps or is missing.
screens.why5: The card names the idea on purpose, and the question is in plain site terms with none of the founder's product talk leaking in.
screens.why6: It's one short question with four short options I can hold in my head, and it says cleanly out loud.
screens.why7: It is an ability with the four ability rungs, two for and two against, and 'I can't tell' as the one escape, but it is anchored on the daily log instead of the site walk where the talking happens, so the occasion bends the measure.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have talked into your phone over the noise on site? Yes, easily · Yes, most of the time · Only sometimes · No · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the noise question, it makes sense to ask whether this thing would have beaten my evening in the trailer.
screens.why2: Trailer, photos, daily logs and punch lists are my words, but 'helped you keep an accurate record of the day's work on site better' is not how I talk, and the 'better' at the end makes me read it twice.
screens.why3: I sit in the trailer uploading photos and typing the log most nights, so I can answer from that.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference and worse cover it with no overlap, and 'I can't tell' fits for a tool I've only heard one line about.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product's plan leaks past the card, but 'keep an accurate record of the day's work on site' is somebody's job description, not words a super would use.
screens.why6: The stem runs well past 20 words with 'uploading photos and typing daily logs and punch lists' plus a long job clause before the 'or not'; it can be said, but it's a mouthful to hold before the four options.
screens.why7: The four fixed answers and the apart escape are right and the belief can be supported or refuted, but the occasion is an ordinary night of doing the log, not the time the log let me down, such as missing notes in a delay dispute, so 'No difference' can mean my night went fine.
screens.instead: Think of the last time a daily log came up short when you needed it, like in a delay dispute. Would Fresco, an AI scribe for site walks, have made that log better, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: It's the last idea question after the card and the 'would it have helped' one, so asking what extra work I'd take on to use it makes sense here.
screens.why2: I get it, but 'who owns each item' isn't how I talk; on site I'd say which sub or who's responsible for each punch item, and 'item' isn't clear when the card only talked about notes.
screens.why3: Calling out which trade has which item on a walk is something I already do, so I know whether I'd say it out loud while filming.
screens.why4: Yes, probably not, no and can't tell are fine, but 'keeps my crew's names private' is odd because items go to subs and companies, not my crew's names, and privacy isn't what would make me do it.
screens.why5: 'Owns each item' sounds like the product's own assignment field leaking through, not words a super uses, though the step itself is still clear.
screens.why6: Short, one question, four options I can hold after one hearing, and one escape at the end.
screens.why7: The step is mine to take, the order is right, the balance works and I can't tell is there, but the Only if condition is about privacy rather than an assurance tied to the effort of naming owners, so the conditional rung bends.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd say which sub has each punch item as you film it. Would you do that, or not? Yes · Only if it builds the punch list for me · Probably not · No · I can't tell

typo_leaks.text: How far back should construction superintendents look for the last time the day's site walks are done and the photoss and notes still have to go into the dailyy log?
